info.short_name: Eastern equine encephalitis virus disease cases
info.long_name: Eastern equine encephalitis virus human disease cases reported to ArboNET
info.short_description: Human Eastern equine encephalitis virus disease cases reported to CDC's ArboNET surveillance system.
info.long_description: Total reported human disease cases of Eastern equine encephalitis virus, including both neuroinvasive and non-neuroinvasive presentations, as reported to CDC's ArboNET national arboviral surveillance system by state and local health departments. Coverage begins in 2003.
info.statement: In {location}, {value} Eastern equine encephalitis virus disease cases were reported in {time}.

info.short_name: Eastern equine encephalitis virus neuroinvasive cases
info.long_name: Eastern equine encephalitis virus human neuroinvasive disease cases reported to ArboNET
info.short_description: Human Eastern equine encephalitis virus neuroinvasive disease cases reported to CDC's ArboNET surveillance system.
info.long_description: Reported human cases of Eastern equine encephalitis virus neuroinvasive disease, meaning cases presenting as meningitis, encephalitis, or acute flaccid paralysis, as reported to CDC's ArboNET national arboviral surveillance system. This is a subset of the total reported case count, so it is always less than or equal to the corresponding arbonet_eee_cases value. Because severe neuroinvasive illness is far more likely to be diagnosed and reported than milder non-neuroinvasive illness, CDC considers neuroinvasive counts the more reliable basis for comparing disease activity across locations and over time. Coverage begins in 2003.
info.statement: In {location}, {value} Eastern equine encephalitis virus neuroinvasive disease cases were reported in {time}.

info.short_name: Eastern equine encephalitis virus non-human activity
info.long_name: Eastern equine encephalitis virus non-human activity reported to ArboNET
info.short_description: Indicator of whether any non-human Eastern equine encephalitis virus activity was reported to CDC for the geography and year.
info.long_description: Binary indicator that equals 1 when veterinary disease cases, or infections in mosquitoes, birds, or sentinel animals, were reported to CDC's ArboNET system for the geography and year, and 0 when no such activity was reported. The value is missing where CDC reports the geography as data unavailable. This measure is not produced for Powassan virus, whose dashboard reports human disease cases only.
info.statement: In {location}, non-human Eastern equine encephalitis virus activity reported in {time}: {value}.

info.short_name: West Nile virus presumptive viremic blood donors
info.long_name: West Nile virus presumptive viremic blood donors identified by blood donor screening
info.short_description: Presumptive viremic blood donors identified through West Nile virus blood donor screening.
info.long_description: Count of presumptive viremic blood donors, defined by CDC as people who had no symptoms at the time of donating blood through a blood collection agency but whose blood tested positive when screened for the presence of West Nile virus. Some presumptive viremic donors go on to develop symptoms after donation. These donors are identified through blood supply screening rather than clinical care, so they are counted separately from the reported human disease cases and are not a subset of them. This measure is reported for West Nile virus only, as it is the only one of these six arboviruses for which routine blood donor screening is conducted.
info.statement: In {location}, {value} West Nile virus presumptive viremic blood donors were identified in {time}.

arbonet_jcv_neuro_cases.long_description: Reported human cases of Jamestown Canyon virus neuroinvasive disease, meaning cases presenting as meningitis, encephalitis, or acute flaccid paralysis, as reported to CDC's ArboNET national arboviral surveillance system. This is a subset of the total reported case count, so it is always less than or equal to the corresponding arbonet_jcv_cases value. Because severe neuroinvasive illness is far more likely to be diagnosed and reported than milder non-neuroinvasive illness, CDC considers neuroinvasive counts the more reliable basis for comparing disease activity across locations and over time. Coverage begins in 2011.
arbonet_jcv_neuro_cases.statement: In {location}, {value} Jamestown Canyon virus neuroinvasive disease cases were reported in {time}.

arbonet_wnv_nonhuman_activity.long_name: West Nile virus non-human activity reported to ArboNET
arbonet_wnv_nonhuman_activity.short_description: Indicator of whether any non-human West Nile virus activity was reported to CDC for the geography and year.
arbonet_wnv_nonhuman_activity.long_description: Binary indicator that equals 1 when veterinary disease cases, or infections in mosquitoes, birds, or sentinel animals, were reported to CDC's ArboNET system for the geography and year, and 0 when no such activity was reported. The value is missing where CDC reports the geography as data unavailable. This measure is not produced for Powassan virus, whose dashboard reports human disease cases only.
arbonet_wnv_nonhuman_activity.statement: In {location}, non-human West Nile virus activity reported in {time}: {value}.

arbonet_wnv_blood_donors.short_name: West Nile virus presumptive viremic blood donors
arbonet_wnv_blood_donors.long_name: West Nile virus presumptive viremic blood donors identified by blood donor screening
arbonet_wnv_blood_donors.short_description: Presumptive viremic blood donors identified through West Nile virus blood donor screening.
arbonet_wnv_blood_donors.long_description: Count of presumptive viremic blood donors, defined by CDC as people who had no symptoms at the time of donating blood through a blood collection agency but whose blood tested positive when screened for the presence of West Nile virus. Some presumptive viremic donors go on to develop symptoms after donation. These donors are identified through blood supply screening rather than clinical care, so they are counted separately from the reported human disease cases and are not a subset of them. This measure is reported for West Nile virus only, as it is the only one of these six arboviruses for which routine blood donor screening is conducted.
arbonet_wnv_blood_donors.statement: In {location}, {value} West Nile virus presumptive viremic blood donors were identified in {time}.

arbonet.name: ArboNET Arboviral Disease Surveillance System
arbonet.organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, Division of Vector-Borne Diseases
arbonet.description: ArboNET is the national arboviral surveillance system managed by CDC together with state and territorial health departments. In addition to human disease, ArboNET maintains data on arboviral infections among presumptive viremic blood donors, veterinary disease cases, mosquitoes, dead birds, and sentinel animals. Human cases are reported by county of residence rather than location of exposure, which is not necessarily the county or state where exposure occurred, and are assigned to the year of illness onset. Several caveats apply: under-reporting is inherent to any surveillance system that depends on clinicians suspecting the disease, ordering the appropriate test, and reporting confirmed results; non-neuroinvasive cases are substantially more under-reported than neuroinvasive cases, so total case counts should not be used to compare disease activity between locations or over time; and there is a lag in reporting to CDC. Values are the counts CDC publishes for public use and are not suppressed or imputed here. Connecticut reported by county through 2022 and by planning region from 2023 onward, so its geography codes change mid-series. Records that CDC assigns to an unallocated placeholder geography (state FIPS plus '999') because the county of residence is unknown are excluded from the county file but retained in the state and national totals. Reporting years differ by disease and the most recent year is preliminary and subject to change.
arbonet.restrictions: Public domain. CDC data is generally not subject to copyright restrictions.
